data.body:
RESEARCH ADDENDUM (2026-05-07): Strategies A & E from review-cycle root-cause analysis

## Empirical evidence supporting per-story PR scope (Strategy A)

PR review history since llm-review CI shipped (commit b8d91d4d, 2026-04-27, ~50 merged PRs through #65):
- ~20 PRs single-cycle, ~15 two-cycle, 10–12 with >2 cycles
- Every >2-cycle PR sampled was >=500 LOC and >=10 files
- Worst offenders: PR #65 (4 rounds, escalated to user with "findings have not converged"), PR #62 (3 rounds, 8->8->6 oscillation), PR #45 and #65 admin-merged with failure conclusion, PR #42 (9 CI failure runs), PR #37 (the 4000-LOC validation case from 6da2-4cff)

Published-research backing:
- SmartBear/Cisco 10-month, 2500-review study: defect-detection effectiveness drops sharply beyond ~200-400 LOC per review; >400-500 LOC/hour produces below-average defect density in 87% of cases
- Google eng-practices: ~100 lines reasonable, 1000 too large; 90% of CLs <10 files; small CLs reviewed in ~1hr vs ~5hr for large
- Bosu/Greiler/Bird (Microsoft): more files in a change -> lower proportion of useful comments
- Bacchelli & Bird (Microsoft, ICSE 2013): understanding-the-change is the dominant reviewer bottleneck
- Conclusion: deeper review of large diffs underperforms; splitting before review is the empirically supported lever

## Considerations for Strategy A (story-level PRs as default)

A1. Hard size gate is the operative mechanism. Block at /dso:commit and at PR open when changed-LOC >400 or files >15 unless explicit --size-override with recorded justification. Story merge becomes default; epic-merge becomes the override path.
A2. Threshold tuning. 400 LOC matches SmartBear; can raise to 600 to match the existing SIZE_WARNING boundary if too aggressive empirically. Target: <=15% of story PRs need override.
A3. Override authority. --size-override at /dso:commit must be a user-confirmed flag; cannot be self-applied by the orchestrator. Justification recorded as a ticket comment for audit.
A4. Interaction with worktree workflow. Per-story PR means each story exits its worktree via merge-to-main-pr.sh independently rather than waiting for the epic close. Sprint orchestrator must accommodate per-story PR creation, not per-epic.
A5. Cross-story dependencies. Stories with depends_on relationships need stacked-PR ordering (the dependent story's PR opens against the dependency's branch, not main). Reference Graphite stacked-diff workflow for the pattern.
A6. Interaction with attestation. The original epic premise (final epic-merge skips re-reviewing already-attested code) may be redundant if every story is its own merged PR — there is no aggregate epic-merge to optimize. Reframe attestation as a hash-stable "this story's review is durable across rebases" rather than "skip re-review at epic close."
A7. Tickets that cannot decompose. Some tasks (large mechanical refactors, schema migrations) genuinely cannot split below 400 LOC. The override path must exist; the goal is making the override visible and rare, not impossible.

## Considerations for Strategy E (true region-splitting in HUGE workflow)

The current REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md does NOT actually split review:
- Step 1-2 sample 7 files via review-sample-files.sh and dispatch 7 haiku pattern-extraction agents
- Step 3 consensus: >=5 matching transformation_description -> CONFIRMED_REFACTOR; else FALLBACK
- Step 4 FALLBACK: passes the WHOLE diff to a single huge-diff-reviewer-{light,standard,deep-arch} agent. This is the gap.
- CONFIRMED_REFACTOR processes per-group anomaly checks via haiku, but only on anomalies — not a general-purpose split

E1. True region split mechanics. For diffs that take FALLBACK, partition by file-group (heuristic: directory + topic clustering, or fixed-size byte budget per region with file-boundary alignment). Each region reviewer sees its slice + summary of out-of-region context.
E2. Dedup pipeline. Region findings flow into a deduplication step keyed on (file:line-range:dimension:claim-fingerprint). Identical findings from overlapping regions collapse to one. Conflicting severity resolves to MAX (sustains rigor).
E3. Cross-region findings. Some bugs only manifest at region boundaries (e.g., caller in region A, callee in region B). Reserve a final synthesis pass (opus arch) that sees all region findings + full diff stat to surface boundary-only issues. This is analogous to the current deep-arch synthesis but applied to FALLBACK.
E4. Interaction with Strategy A. If A succeeds, E becomes lower-priority — most PRs will be small enough that HUGE never triggers. E remains necessary for the override-path PRs and for any retroactive review of pre-A epic-merges.
E5. Pattern-extraction phase preserved. Step 1-2 of HUGE remains valuable for CONFIRMED_REFACTOR routing — that path empirically reduces volume. Only FALLBACK needs rework.
E6. Cross-region finding examples to watch for: type signature changes whose callers are in different regions; shared mutable state introduced in one region and read in another; security-relevant validation removed in one file and depended on in another.

## Implementation sequencing recommendation

1. Strategy A (size gate + per-story PR default) ships first — highest-leverage lever.
2. Strategy E (HUGE workflow region-split) follows — necessary for the override path and historical PRs.
3. Both strategies depend on the stateful-re-review epic (B+F) being designed first, because per-story PRs and region reviews both benefit from the prior-findings/defenses substrate.

## Source references

- SmartBear "11 Best Practices for Peer Code Review"
- Cisco case study (SmartBear 10-month / 2500-review study)
- Bacchelli & Bird "Expectations, Outcomes, and Challenges of Modern Code Review" ICSE 2013
- Bosu/Greiler/Bird "Characteristics of Useful Code Reviews" Microsoft Research
- Google eng-practices: review/developer/small-cls.html
- Graphite: stacked-PR best practices
